title: Exterior coherent cohomology of abelian spaces and universal base change
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $a:A\to S$ be a proper smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space], with geometric fibres smooth proper geometrically connected group schemes. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; smoothness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every scheme $T$ over $S$, with no Noetherian or reducedness assumption, put $f:A_T=A\times_ST\to T$. On the small etale sites take structure-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; $R^if_*\mathcal O_{A_T}$ denotes the $i$th right derived module direct image, and cohomology is right derived global sections of the underlying additive sheaf. Then $\mathcal O_T\to f_*\mathcal O_{A_T}$ is an isomorphism, $V_T=R^1f_*\mathcal O_{A_T}$ is finite locally free (Zariski locally $\mathcal O_T^g$ with $g$ finite), and the relative cup product [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product] gives isomorphisms of graded $\mathcal O_T$-algebras
$$\bigwedge\nolimits^*_{\mathcal O_T}V_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{i\geq0}R^if_*\mathcal O_{A_T}.$$
Here the exterior algebra is the tensor algebra modulo the ideal generated by $v\otimes v$; its degree-$i$ map sends $v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_i$ to $v_1\smile\cdots\smile v_i$. These identifications commute with every base change $T'\to T$ via the canonical higher-direct-image comparison, including nonflat base changes. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ they induce $H^0(A_T,\mathcal O)=R$ and cup-product isomorphisms $\bigwedge_R^i V\simeq H^i(A_T,\mathcal O)$, where $V=H^1(A_T,\mathcal O)$ satisfies $\widetilde V=V_T$ and is a finite projective $R$-module (a direct summand of a finite free module). Thus all $H^i(A_T,\mathcal O)$ are finite projective and vanish for sufficiently large $i$. No smoothness or representability hypothesis on a dual Picard functor is assumed.

source.place: I Remark 8.7(e), printed p.37, and I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, for the field dimension/Hopf inputs only. The relative coherent exterior-algebra and universal base-change assertion here is an agent-stated prerequisite; Milne does not state this relative theorem. WANTED: Mumford–Fogarty–Kirwan, Geometric Invariant Theory, Chapter 6, coherent cohomology of abelian schemes in the prerequisites to Proposition 6.7, including extension to abelian algebraic spaces.

proof.text: On etale scheme charts smoothness gives flatness by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Thus $a$ is flat. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], every $A_T\to T$ is flat, proper and finitely presented, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Each geometric fibre is a proper smooth connected group scheme over an algebraically closed field, so [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] makes it geometrically integral, in particular reduced; it is connected by hypothesis and nonempty because of the identity section. Apply [lem-sfb-space-geometric-h0]: $\mathcal O_T\to f_*\mathcal O_{A_T}$ is the canonical isomorphism for every $T$, including nonreduced $T$.

source.place: Tag 0E0S (lemma-proper-flat-geom-red-connected); chart flatness and base-change hypotheses.

proof.text: Work over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, so $R$ is Noetherian. The module $\mathcal O_{A_U}$ is quasi-coherent of finite presentation (free of rank one over itself) and flat over $U$ by step 1. Thus [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change] applies with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_{A_U}$. It gives a Zariski perfect complex $K_U=R\epsilon_{U,*}Ra_{U,*}\mathcal O_{A_U}$ and its canonical small-etale counit identification with $Ra_{U,*}\mathcal O_{A_U}$. By [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective], $K_U$ is represented by the tilde of a bounded finite-projective $R$-complex. The equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], whose inverse is derived global sections, identifies this with the perfect $R$-complex $K=R\Gamma(A_U,\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Tag 0CTM (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), Zariski convention via 071Q and 08HG; perfect affine model Tag 08EB and affine equivalence 06Z0.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-external-cup] on all finite powers of $A_U$. On $K$ let $\mu$ be cup product, $u$ structural pullback, $\varepsilon=e^*$ at the identity section, and $\Delta=\kappa_{A_U,A_U}^{-1}m^*$ for the group law $m$. Naturality identifies the pullbacks of the two group identities $m(m\times1)=m(1\times m)$ and $m(e\times1)=m(1\times e)=1$ with coassociativity and the two counit identities for $\Delta$. Since $m^*$ and $e^*$ preserve products and units and $\kappa$ is multiplicative, $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$ are algebra maps. Thus $K$ is a commutative bialgebra object in $D(R)$. For every $R\to B$, the same node identifies $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ with $R\Gamma(A_B,\mathcal O)$ as a bialgebra object, via the canonical comparison.

source.place: Tags 08IN, 08IR; the formal bialgebra diagrams from the group identities and the coherent external cup comparisons.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$. Its fibre $G=A_\Omega$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected group scheme, hence an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]; [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] makes it geometrically integral. Put $g=\dim G$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-structure-h1-dimension], $\dim_\Omega H^1(G,\mathcal O)=g$. Proper coherent finiteness [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional] makes each $H^i$ finite dimensional. The finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $G$ is Noetherian, and [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^i=0$ for $i>g$. The bialgebra [lem-sfb-coherent-group-bialgebra] has $H^0=\Omega$, the signed product and the required coproduct and counit. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-bialgebra-top-degree-exterior] over the algebraically closed, hence perfect, field $\Omega$: the actual multiplication identifies its coherent cohomology with $\bigwedge^*H^1$. By the scheme comparison in [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-external-cup], this is precisely the residue bialgebra of step 3, with the small-etale cup product.

source.place: I Remark 8.7(e), printed p.37; I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, applied to coherent rather than constant-coefficient cohomology; vanishing Tag 02UZ.

proof.text: For a point $s\in U$, set $R_s=\mathcal O_{U,s}$ and $k_s=\kappa(s)$. The perfect complex $K_s=R_s\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ has the bialgebra maps of step 3. Field extension from $k_s$ to an algebraic closure is faithfully flat; cohomology of a complex of vector spaces and its cup maps commute with this extension. Step 4 therefore says already over $k_s$ that the product on $H^*(k_s\otimes_{R_s}^{\mathbf L}K_s)$ is exterior on degree one: squares vanish after the injective scalar extension, and the kernel and cokernel of each exterior-product map become zero. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-derived-bialgebra-exterior-rigidity] to $K_s$. It has a bounded finite free zero-differential model, $H^1(K_s)$ is free, and cup product is exterior on it. This is an application to a Noetherian local ring; no smoothness of a relative Picard functor is used.

source.place: Agent assembly: local bialgebra rigidity (minimal models Tag 0BCC and maximal-ideal separatedness Tag 00IP); faithfully flat field descent of finite-dimensional linear maps.

proof.text: The isomorphism at $s$ spreads to a principal neighbourhood. Indeed write $K$ as its bounded finite-projective model $P$ and let $E$ be the bounded zero-differential complex of finite free $R$-modules with the ranks given by step 5 at $s$. The directed system of rings $R_f$, with $f\notin\mathfrak p_s$ and refinements by products, has colimit $R_s$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-perfect-hom-colimit] to $P,E$: the two inverse derived isomorphisms over $R_s$ lift to some $R_f$, and their two composite equalities lift after a further refinement by the injectivity part of that same colimit bijection. Thus $K|_{D(f)}\simeq E|_{D(f)}$, and all its cohomology modules are finite free there. Since $s$ was arbitrary, the sheaves $R^ia_*\mathcal O_A$ are Zariski finite locally free. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-relative-cup-sections](i) for $A_{D(f)}\to D(f)$, the relative cup product on sections over $D(f)$ is the cup product of $H^*(A_{D(f)},\mathcal O)$, which is $H^*(K)_f$ with its product by the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-external-cup] for $R\to R_f$; by part (ii) for the open immersions $D(fh)\subseteq D(f)$ these identifications commute with restriction. Hence at each Zariski stalk the relative cup product is the product of $H^*(K_s)$, and the square-zero identities and exterior-product isomorphisms of step 5 hold at every Zariski stalk. So squares of local sections are zero and the canonical wedge maps of relative cup products are isomorphisms: their kernels and cokernels have all stalks zero. This establishes the exterior algebra assertion over $S$, with $V_S=R^1a_*\mathcal O_A$.

source.place: Agent assembly using perfect Hom continuity for the localization system; finite-free model at each point from local bialgebra rigidity.

proof.text: For arbitrary $g:T\to S$, [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change] gives the canonical isomorphism $Lg^*Ra_*\mathcal O_A\simeq Rf_*\mathcal O_{A_T}$. On each zero-differential finite free chart from step 6, $Lg^*$ is ordinary tensor on that model and the differentials remain zero for every base map. Thus its degree-$i$ map is precisely $g^*R^ia_*\mathcal O_A\xrightarrow{\sim}R^if_*\mathcal O_{A_T}$, including nonflat $g$. Product compatibility: for an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $T$ mapping into a principal open $D(f)$ of $S$, [lem-sfb-space-affine-relative-cup-sections](i),(ii) for $\operatorname{Spec}B\to D(f)$ identify the relative cup products with the global ones and the base-change map on sections with the pullback $H^i(A_{D(f)},\mathcal O)\to H^i(A_B,\mathcal O)$, i.e. with the comparison $B\otimes_{R_f}^{\mathbf L}K_f\to R\Gamma(A_B,\mathcal O)$, which respects products by [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-external-cup]. So both sides send $1\otimes(v_1\smile\cdots\smile v_i)$ to the cup of the pulled-back classes. These formulas determine the wedge maps and glue. Applied to $T'\to T$, identity and composition coherence of the derived comparisons shows that the resulting isomorphisms are the canonical higher-direct-image comparisons requested in the statement. No Noetherian or reducedness assumption on $T$ or $T'$ entered this tensor calculation.

source.place: Tag 08IR and cup compatibility sites-cohomology Tag 0H9A; cohomology of the local zero-differential free model.

proof.text: If $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, use [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections] with $M=\mathcal O_{A_T}$ to identify $H^i(A_T,\mathcal O)$ with $\Gamma(T,R^if_*\mathcal O)$. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], the latter sheaf is the etale association of its Zariski quasi-coherent module, whose affine associated-module description gives $\widetilde{H^i}=R^if_*\mathcal O$. By [lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective], these sections, in particular $V=H^1$, are finite projective. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-relative-cup-sections](i),(ii) these identifications carry the global cup product to the relative one and commute with restriction to principal opens. The wedge comparison on sections is an isomorphism: localize at a finite principal cover trivializing $V_T$, where it sends each ordered basis wedge to the corresponding cup product; these maps agree on overlaps. This gives exactly $\bigwedge_R^iV\simeq H^i$, including $H^0=R$. A finite trivializing cover of the quasi-compact affine $T$ bounds the local ranks of $V_T$ by some finite $N$, so the ordered-wedge bases show $\bigwedge^iV_T=0$ for $i>N$. Hence $H^i=0$ for $i>N$. The empty affine scheme (zero ring) and rank zero give the same formulas.

source.place: Affine higher-image sections Tag 08EX; affine finite locally free sections are finite projective. Ordered-basis wedge calculation and finite cover bound.

proof_origin.place: Assembly of proper flat perfect pushforward 0CTM, coherent bialgebra fibre calculation using Milne I 12.2, local derived-bialgebra rigidity, and arbitrary derived base change 08IR. The relative theorem is not stated in Milne.
